The issue is a little more complicated than the title lets on. You have to understand how open carry works in Michigan. In most states that allow open carry, a law was specifically passed detailing the rights to open carry. However, in Michigan, open carry is allowed because there is no law allowing or disallowing it. It's a legal void in Michigan. There are no laws or regulations about open carrying a firearm at all, which if you subscribe to the plain language of the 2nd amendment (which I personally favor), that's how it should be. In contrast, concealed-carry in Michigan has a specific law that enabled it along with all the regulations that govern the permit holder.

The problem presented in the case before the court was that the State of Michigan also delegated some legislative power to the smaller branches of government such as schools and municipalities. The law on CCW forbids a permit holder from taking their firearm into a school. No such law exists for open carry. However, the legislative powers that the State gave to the smaller branches of government allow the schools, in particular, to decide for themselves whether to allow firearms or not. As one can imagine, most, if not all, school districts banned firearms.

Thus the legal question became which legal power is trump when a person open carries on school property? The majority of the court (it was a 5-4 decision) said that the State legislature could have prohibited the schools from making such a rule if it wanted by not delegating that decision to the schools but the legislature didn't do so.
